Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 59, verses 1–2:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Glorifies Allah whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ (1)

By His saying, exalted is His praise, ﴿Glorifies Allah﴾: prays to Allah and prostrates to Him; ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of His creation; ﴿and He is the Almighty, the Wise﴾: He says, "He is Almighty in His retribution against those among His creatures whom He punishes for disobeying Him, and Wise in His management of them."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think that they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O you who have vision.﴾ (2)

By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾: Allah is the One who expelled those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ from among the People of the Book, namely the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, from their homes, meaning their leaving their dwellings and abodes, when they made a treaty with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he would grant them safety for their lives, their women and their children, and that they would have what the camels could carry of their property, and that their houses and the rest of their property would be left to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted this from them, so they left their homes; some of them went to Syria and some went to Khaybar. That is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾, he said: "The Nadir," up to His saying: ﴿and to disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾.

Mention of what lies between all of that concerning them:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾, it was said: "[to] Syria. They were Banu al-Nadir, a tribe of the Jews, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ expelled them from Medina to Khaybar on his return from Uhud."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, ﴿from their homes at the first gathering﴾, he said: "They were Banu al-Nadir, whom the Prophet ﷺ fought until they made peace with him on condition of exile, so he expelled them to Syria, and on condition that they could have what the camels carried of anything except the hilqa, and the hilqa is the weapons. They were from a tribe that had not been exiled in the past, and Allah, mighty and majestic, had decreed exile for them; had it not been so, He would have punished them in this world with killing and captivity."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾, he said: "These are the Nadir, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ expelled them."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: "The whole Surah al-Hashr was revealed concerning Banu al-Nadir, mentioning what Allah, mighty and majestic, afflicted them with of His vengeance, and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was empowered against them with, and what he did with them. So He said: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾ ... the verses."

* *

And His saying: ﴿at the first gathering﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: at the first assembling in this world, and that is their gathering to the land of Syria.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding His saying: ﴿at the first gathering﴾, he said: "Their exile was the first gathering in this world, to Syria."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "A fire will come from the east of the earth, gathering people to its west; it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, rest with them wherever they rest, and it will devour whoever lags behind."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: "It reached me that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ exiled Banu al-Nadir, he said: 'Go forth, for this is the first gathering, and we are on your trail.'"

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿at the first gathering﴾, he said: "Syria, when He returned them to Syria," and he recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what you already have, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their heels﴾, he said: "From where they came; their heels were turned back when they returned to Syria, and from where they came they were sent back to it."

* *

And His saying: ﴿You did not think that they would leave﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: you did not think that these whom Allah expelled from their homes among the People of the Book would leave their dwellings and abodes; ﴿and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah﴾. It is mentioned that the people's thinking was only that Abdullah ibn Ubayy and a group of hypocrites sent to them when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them, urging them to stand firm in their fortresses and promising them victory.

As:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, that a group from Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, among them Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Wadi'a and Malik, the two sons of Nawfal, and Suwayd and Da'is, sent to Banu al-Nadir: "Stand firm and defend yourselves, for we will not abandon you; if you are fought, we will fight alongside you, and if you go out, we will go out with you." So they waited for their help, but they did not do it, and they had fortified themselves in the fortresses against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he descended upon them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿But Allah came at them from where they did not expect﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the command of Allah came to them from where they did not reckon it would reach them, and that command which came to them from Allah where they did not expect it was that He cast terror into their hearts by the descent of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon them with his companions. His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿and He cast terror into their hearts﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾

By His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿They destroyed their homes﴾ he means Banu al-Nadir from among the Jews, and that they were destroying their dwellings; this was because they used to look, as it is mentioned, at the beam in their houses that pleased them, or the pillar or the door, and they would pull it out with their hands and the hands of the believers.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾: "They began to destroy them from their insides, and the believers began to destroy them from their outsides."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: "When they made peace with the Prophet ﷺ, they would not leave any beam that pleased them without taking it, and that was their destruction." Qatada said: "The Muslims would destroy what was adjacent to them from the outside, and the Jews would destroy it from the inside."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: "Banu al-Nadir carried away from their property whatever the camels could bear. A man among them would tear down his house from the frame of its door, place it on the back of his camel and set off with it." He said: "That is His saying: ﴿They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾, and that was their demolishing of their houses from the frames of their doors when they carried them away."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾, he said: "These are the Nadir. The Prophet ﷺ made peace with them on what the camels could carry, so they began to pull up the pegs, destroying their houses."

Others said: "It was only said thus because they used to destroy their homes in order to build with their materials what the Muslims had demolished of their fortresses."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers, so take warning, O you who have vision﴾, he said: "He means Banu al-Nadir. Whenever the Muslims demolished some of their fortresses, they would begin to tear down and destroy their houses, and then build with what the Muslims had destroyed; that was their ruin."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿They destroyed their homes by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾, "He means the people of the Nadir: whenever the Muslims demolished something of their fortress, they would begin to tear down their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers, and then build what the Muslims had destroyed."

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of the readers of the Hijaz, Medina and Iraq, except Abu Amr, recited ﴿yukhribūna﴾ with a light rā', meaning they leave them and abandon them as ruins; and Abu Amr used to recite it ﴿yukharribūna﴾ with a doubled rā', meaning they demolish their houses. It is mentioned that Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Hasan al-Basri used to recite it similarly to Abu Amr's reading. Abu Amr, as is reported from him, claimed that he chose the doubling of the rā' because, as I have mentioned, ikhrab is only leaving something in ruin without an occupant, whereas the Banu al-Nadir did not abandon their dwellings so as to move away from them; rather, they ruined them by tearing down and demolishing, and that, in his view, can only be expressed with the doubled form.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites it with the light rā', because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it. Some people knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs used to say: "al-takhrib and al-ikhrab have one meaning; the difference is only in the wording, not in the meaning."

* *

And His saying: ﴿So take warning, O you who have vision﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So be admonished, O assembly of people of understanding, by what Allah brought down upon these Jews whom Allah cast terror into their hearts, while they were in their fortresses, of His vengeance; and know that Allah is the Ally of whoever allies with Him, and the Helper of His Messenger against everyone who opposes him, and that He will bring down upon whoever deserves His vengeance the like of what He brought down upon Banu al-Nadir. By "those with vision" in this place He means the vision of the hearts, for taking warning is done with it rather than with the sight of the eyes.

And whoever opposes Allah – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty﴾ (4).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Had Allah not decreed and prescribed for these Jews of Banu al-Nadir, in the Mother of the Book, exile (al-jala', which is moving from one place to another, and from one town to another).

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾: it is the departure of people from one land to another land.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾: al-jala' is their expulsion from their land to another land. He said: It is also said: al-jala' is flight. From it one says: "jalla al-qawm min manazilihim" (the people went out from their dwellings), and "ajlaytuhum ana" (I expelled them).

* *

And His saying: ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾ from their land and their homes, He would have punished them in this world by killing and captivity. But He lifted the punishment from them in this world by killing, and made their punishment in this world to be exile. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, in addition to what befell them of the humiliation of this world through exile from their land and their dwellings.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: The Nadir were from a tribe that had not suffered exile in times past, and Allah had decreed exile upon them; and had it not been for that, He would have punished them in this world by killing and captivity.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, concerning ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾, and there was for them a vengeance from Allah, ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾: that is, by the sword, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, in addition to that.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had besieged them until he reached every extent with them. They then gave him what he wanted from them, so he made peace with them on condition that he would spare their lives, and expel them from their land and homelands, and send them to Adhri'at in Syria; and he assigned for every three of them a camel and a water-skin.

It is related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾: the people of al-Nadir. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them until he reached every extent with them, and they gave the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) what he desired. Then he mentioned something similar and added in it: "This is the exile."

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: That which Allah did to these Jews, what He did to them of expelling them from their homes and casting terror into their hearts from the believers, and making for them in the Hereafter the punishment of the Fire, is because of what they themselves did in this world of opposing Allah and His Messenger in His command and prohibition, and disobeying their Lord in what He commanded them of following Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And whoever opposes Allah – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: whoever opposes Allah in His command and prohibition, indeed Allah is severe in penalty.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 59, verses 3–4:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾ (3) ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty﴾ (4).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Had Allah not decreed and prescribed for these Jews of Banu al-Nadir, in the Mother of the Book, exile (al-jala', which is moving from one place to another, and from one town to another).

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾: it is the departure of people from one land to another land.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾: al-jala' is their expulsion from their land to another land. He said: It is also said: al-jala' is flight. From it one says: "jalla al-qawm min manazilihim" (the people went out from their dwellings), and "ajlaytuhum ana" (I expelled them).

* *

And His saying: ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾ from their land and their homes, He would have punished them in this world by killing and captivity. But He lifted the punishment from them in this world by killing, and made their punishment in this world to be exile. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, in addition to what befell them of the humiliation of this world through exile from their land and their dwellings.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: The Nadir were from a tribe that had not suffered exile in times past, and Allah had decreed exile upon them; and had it not been for that, He would have punished them in this world by killing and captivity.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, concerning ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾, and there was for them a vengeance from Allah, ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾: that is, by the sword, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, in addition to that.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had besieged them until he reached every extent with them. They then gave him what he wanted from them, so he made peace with them on condition that he would spare their lives, and expel them from their land and homelands, and send them to Adhri'at in Syria; and he assigned for every three of them a camel and a water-skin.

It is related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾: the people of al-Nadir. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them until he reached every extent with them, and they gave the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) what he desired. Then he mentioned something similar and added in it: "This is the exile."

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: That which Allah did to these Jews, what He did to them of expelling them from their homes and casting terror into their hearts from the believers, and making for them in the Hereafter the punishment of the Fire, is because of what they themselves did in this world of opposing Allah and His Messenger in His command and prohibition, and disobeying their Lord in what He commanded them of following Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And whoever opposes Allah – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: whoever opposes Allah in His command and prohibition, indeed Allah is severe in penalty.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 5:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing upon their roots — it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Whatever varieties of palm trees you cut down, or left standing upon their roots.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of al-līnah (the word for palm trees here). Some of them said: it refers to all kinds of palm trees except the ajwah (a superior variety of date).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrimah, regarding ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "the palm tree."

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing﴾: "al-līnah is what is other than the ajwah of the palm trees."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "al-līnah is what differs from the ajwah of the dates."

- And he narrated it to us another time, and said: "of the palm trees."

- Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "all the palm trees except the ajwah."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾, and al-līnah: "what is other than the ajwah of the palm trees."

- Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri: ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: "all varieties of palm trees except the ajwah."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "the palm tree other than the ajwah."

Others said: all palm trees are līnah, both the ajwah among them and non-ajwah.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "the palm tree."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "a palm tree." He said: Some of the Emigrants (muhajirun) forbade others from cutting down the palm trees, and they said: "They are only the spoils of the Muslims." The Quran was revealed confirming the one who forbade cutting them, and declaring the one who cut them free of sin; and cutting them and leaving them was by His permission.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: he said, "the palm tree."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: "al-līnah is the palm tree, whether ajwah or otherwise." Allah said, ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: "What they cut down of the palm trees of al-Nadir, when al-Nadir betrayed."

Others said: it is a type of palm tree.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: "al-līnah: a type of palm tree."

Others said: they are the noble palm trees.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us regarding ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾: "of the noble palm trees among them."

The correct view on this matter is the view of the one who said: al-līnah is the palm tree, and these are among the varieties of palm trees as long as they are not ajwah. It is to these that Dhu al-Rummah referred in his saying:

"The wings of a flock of birds settling upon a palm tree (līnah), its dew of night glistening on its feathers."[[The line is by Dhu al-Rummah (Lisan al-ʿArab: r-y-ʿ), where the narration has "ruyaʿah" in place of "līnah." Al-līnah: the palm tree, and every palm tree other than the ajwah is of al-līn. The author previously cited this line at His saying "Do you build on every high place a sign" (26:128), and we explained it there in detail, so refer to it there (19:93).]] Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: al-līnah is from al-lawn (the colour/kind), and al-liyan is the plural, and its singular is al-līnah. He said: It was named līnah because it is a fiʿlah from fiʿl, which is lawn, and it is a kind of palm tree; but when the letter before it was broken, it was changed into a yāʾ. Some of them denied this view and said: if it were as he said, they would have pluralized it as al-lawan, not al-liyan. And some grammarians of Kufa used to say: the plural of līnah is līn.

It is related that this verse was revealed for the following reason: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut down the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and burned them, Banu al-Nadir said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "You used to forbid corruption and condemn it, so why do you cut down our palm trees and burn them?" Then Allah revealed this verse, informing them that whatever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut down or left, it was by the command of Allah that he acted.

Others said: rather, this was revealed because of a disagreement that arose among the Muslims about cutting them down and leaving them.

Those who said that it was revealed because of what the Jews said to the Muslims:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to us, saying: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came upon them, meaning Banu al-Nadir, they barricaded themselves from him in their fortresses. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the cutting of the palm trees and burning them. They called out to him: "O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption and condemn it in those who committed it, so what is this cutting down and burning of palm trees?" Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing upon their roots — it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.﴾

Those who said: it was revealed because of a disagreement that existed among the Muslims regarding this matter:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing﴾ ... the verse, meaning that He might admonish them. The Muslims that day cut down the palm trees, and others refrained, out of dislike that it would be corruption. The Jews said: "Did Allah permit you to commit corruption?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down﴾.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing upon their roots﴾: he said, "Some of the Emigrants forbade others from cutting down the palm trees, and they said: 'They are only the spoils of the Muslims.' The Quran was revealed confirming the one who forbade cutting them, and declaring the one who cut them free of sin; and cutting them and leaving them was by His permission."

- Sulayman ibn ʿUmar ibn Khalid al-Barqi narrated to us, saying Ibn al-Mubarak narrated, from Musa ibn ʿUqbah, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut down the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir, and concerning that ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾ ... the verse was revealed. And concerning that Hassan ibn Thabit said:

"And it became easy for the nobles of Banu Lu'ay the burning at al-Buwayrah, spreading far."[[The line is by Hassan ibn Thabit (Mu'jam ma Ista'jam by al-Bakri: rasm al-Buwayrah 285). He said al-Buwayrah, with a short initial vowel and the unpointed r, in diminutive form; it is from Tayma. Abu ʿUbaydah said in the Kitab al-Amwal: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and cut down the palm trees (zahw) of al-Buwayrah, and concerning them it was revealed: "Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing upon their roots — it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient." Hassan said: "It became easy for the nobles..." the line. Hassan said that because the Quraysh were those who pressured Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the holder of the pact of Banu Qurayzah, to break the agreement between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he went out with them to the Trench, and at that point the trial and fear grew severe for the Muslims. End.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾:

He says: By the command of Allah you cut what you cut and left what you left, and so that He would enrage His enemies by that; and it was not corruption.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, regarding ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾: "that is, by the command of Allah it was cut, and it was not corruption, but a punishment from Allah; and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾:

And so that He might humble those who go outside the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, opposing His command and prohibition, and they are the Jews of Banu al-Nadir.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 6:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them — you did not spur upon it any horses or camels. But Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: that which Allah returned to His Messenger from them, meaning from the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir. It is said of this: "faa'a al-shay' 'ala fulan" means it returned to him, and "afa'tu-hu 'alayhi" means I returned it to him. It has also been said that by this He meant the wealth of Qurayzah. ﴿So you did not spur upon it any horses or camels﴾ means: you did not urge toward it any horses or camels, and ruka'ib (riding camels) are the camels. The Exalted described what Allah returned to His Messenger from them as that over which no horses were spurred, because the Muslims did not face battle over it and did not exert effort for it; rather, the people were with them and in their own land, so there was no spurring of horses or camels.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them — you did not spur upon it any horses or camels﴾ ... the verse, he said: You did not cross a valley toward it, nor did you travel toward it by journey. Rather, it was orchards of the Banu al-Nadir, a provision which Allah gave to His Messenger. It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Any town which submits to Allah and His Messenger belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and any town which the Muslims conquer by force, then one-fifth of it is for Allah and His Messenger, and what remains is booty for those who fought over it."

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding His words: ﴿so you did not spur upon it any horses or camels﴾, he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) made peace with the people of Fadak and villages he named, which I do not remember, while he was besieging another people, and they sent to him seeking peace. He said: ﴿so you did not spur upon it any horses or camels﴾ means: without fighting. Al-Zuhri said: The Banu al-Nadir were exclusively for the Prophet (ﷺ), as they did not conquer them by force, but by agreement, and the Prophet (ﷺ) divided them among the Muhajirun, giving the Ansar nothing of them except two men who had need.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ruman: ﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them﴾, meaning the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿so you did not spur upon it any horses or camels, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿so you did not spur upon it any horses or camels﴾, he said: Their Lord mentions that He gave them victory and sufficed them without cavalry, and without preparation, in Qurayzah and Khaybar. What Allah restored to His Messenger from Qurayzah, he gave it to the emigrant women of Quraysh.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them — you did not spur upon it any horses or camels, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ He said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet to march toward Qurayzah and al-Nadir, and the Muslims at that time did not have many horses or camels, so He made what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) obtained subject to his judgment as he willed, and there were no horses or camels that day to be spurred. He said: Al-iyjaf is to hasten the journey, and it belongs to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). From this came Khaybar, Fadak, and Arabian villages. Allah commanded His Messenger to prepare for Yanbu', and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to it and took all of it. Some people said: Why did he not divide it? So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed His excuse, saying: (﻿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near kindred and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer) Then He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ ... the verse.

- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿so you did not spur upon it any horses or camels﴾: He means the day of Qurayzah.

* *

And His words: ﴿But Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills﴾

He informs you that just as He gave Muhammad (ﷺ) power over the Banu al-Nadir, He, the Exalted, reports by this that what Allah restored to him of wealth, over which the Muslims did not spur horses or camels against the enemies, which they agreed upon with him, is specifically his, to be managed as he sees fit. He means: Muhammad (ﷺ) only received the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir by agreement, not by force, so no division takes place in it. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ means: Allah is over every thing He intends, possessing power that nothing can frustrate, and by His power over what He wills, He gave His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) power over the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir, and he took possession of it from them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 7:

The interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the traveller, so that it does not circulate merely among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ (7)

By His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, [He means] that which Allah, mighty and majestic, returned to His Messenger from the property of the polytheists of the towns.

The scholars differed concerning what is meant by this verse among the various opinions. Some of them said: it means the jizya (poll-tax) and the kharaj (land-tax).

Those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: ﴿The alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾ until he reached ﴿All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, then said: this is for these. Then he said: ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything, indeed one-fifth of it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near of kin﴾ ... the verse, then said: this verse is for these. Then he recited: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor emigrants and those who were expelled from their homes and property, seeking bounty from Allah and approval, and helping Allah and His Messenger; those are the truthful﴾ [and] ﴿those who were settled in the abode and in the faith before them﴾ and ﴿those who came after them﴾, then said: this verse has encompassed the Muslims in general, so there is no one except that he has a right to it. Then he said: If I live, the shepherd who drives his donkeys will certainly come to receive his share, without his brow having sweated for it.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us concerning His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ until [[The word "until" may be an addition by the copyists.]] it reached me that it is the jizya, and the kharaj: the kharaj of the people of the towns.

Others said: it means the spoil that the Muslims obtain from their enemy, from the people of war, by fighting by force.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, concerning ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾: it is what the Muslims gain by horse and riding-camel, and what is conquered by war by force; ﴿belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the traveller, so that it does not circulate merely among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾. He said: this is another division of what is obtained by war, among the Muslims, according to what Allah has set for it.

Others said: it means the spoil that the Muslims gained by horse and riding-camel and was taken by overpowering. They said: the spoils in the early days of Islam belonged to those whom Allah named in these verses, to the exclusion of those who pressed on them, and then this was abrogated by the verse in Surat al-Anfal.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the traveller﴾: He said: the fay' was for these, then that was abrogated in Surat al-Anfal, where He said: ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything, indeed one-fifth of it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the traveller﴾. So this abrogated what preceded it in Surat al-Anfal, and the one-fifth was assigned to those who had the fay' in Surat al-Hashr. The spoil was divided into five-fifths: four-fifths for those who fought for it, and the remaining fifth was divided into five parts: one part for Allah and the Messenger, one part for the kin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime, one part for the orphans, one part for the needy, and one part for the traveller. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) directed these two shares: the share of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the share of his kin, and they spent them on the path of Allah as charity on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Others said: it means what the people of war made peace with the Muslims concerning their property. They said: His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾ ... the verses, explains the division of the property that Allah mentioned in the verse before this verse, which is His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not press on it with horse or riding-camel﴾. This is a view that some of the later jurists used to hold.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that the ruling of this verse is different from the ruling of the verse before it. That is because the property in the verse before it is what Allah, mighty and majestic, made exclusively for His Messenger (ﷺ) to the exclusion of others, and He did not give anyone a share in it. This is what came in the report from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) sent for me, so I entered upon him, and he said: Some men of your people's households have come, and we have ordered a small gift for them, so distribute it among them. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, command someone other than me to do it. He said: Take it, O man. While I was like that, Yarfa', his freedman, came and said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Zubayr, Uthman and Sa'd are asking permission. He said: Admit them. Then he waited a while and came back and said: This is Ali and al-Abbas asking permission. He said: Admit them both. When al-Abbas entered he said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this treacherous, deceitful, wicked man. They had come disputing about what Allah had restored to His Messenger from the properties of the Banu al-Nadir. The people said: Judge between them, O Commander of the Faithful, and relieve each of them from the other, for their dispute has gone on too long. He said: I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity"? They said: He did say that. Then he said to them both: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that? They both said: Yes. He said: I will inform you about this fay'. Allah singled out His Prophet (ﷺ) with something He gave no one else: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not press on it with horse or riding-camel﴾. So this was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). By Allah, he did not hoard it from you, nor did he keep it to himself to the exclusion of you; indeed he distributed it among you until this property remained, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would spend from it on his family for their year, then he would place what remained in the property of Allah. So when the preceding verse had passed, mentioning the property which Allah singled out for His Messenger (ﷺ), giving no one a share along with him, and this verse was a report about the property which Allah made for various categories, it became known that the property He made for categories of His creation is other than the property He made for the Prophet (ﷺ) exclusively, and He made no partner with him in it.

* *

His saying: ﴿and to the near of kin﴾

He says: and to the near of kin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and the orphans, who are the needy children of the Muslims who have no property; and the needy, who are those who combine poverty and the humiliation of asking; and the traveller, who are the wayfarers cut off from their means, in a journey not in disobedience to Allah, mighty and majestic.

We have already mentioned the reports that came from the people of interpretation regarding the explanation of this earlier in our book.

* *

His saying: ﴿so that it does not circulate merely among the rich among you﴾

He, mighty is His praise, says: And We made what He restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns for these categories, so that this fay' would not be a circulating wealth passed around among the rich among you, one spending it this time on his own needs and another time on the avenues of righteousness and the paths of goodness, so that they would place it wherever they wished. Rather, We set in it a sunnah that does not change or alter.

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of the readers of the regions, apart from Abu Ja'far the reciter, read ﴿kay la yakuna﴾ and ﴿dawlah﴾ with a fatha on the latter, according to the meaning I have described, and that the subject is the fay'.

* *

His saying: ﴿dawlah﴾

It is the accusative as the predicate of "yakun". Abu Ja'far the reciter read ﴿kay la takuna dawlatun﴾ with the dawlah in the nominative, governed by "takun", and the predicate is His saying: ﴿between the rich among you﴾. As for the dal of ﴿dawlah﴾ with a damma, all the readers of the regions read it so, except that it is related from Abu Abd al-Rahman that he read it with a fatha.

The people of knowledge of Arabic speech differed concerning the meaning of this, whether the dal is read with a damma or a fatha. Some of the Kufans said: the meaning is that when it is read with a fatha, dawlah means that the army takes turns, one defeating another, then the defeater is defeated, and it is said: the dawlah has returned to these. He said: and dawlah with a damma refers to rule and the years that change and alternate over time; so that is "dawlah" and "duwal". Others said: the difference between the damma and the fatha is that dawlah (with fatha) is the name of the thing that circulates in its own form, and dawlah (with damma) is the act.

The reading I do not permit other than in this matter is ﴿kay la yakuna﴾ with the ya', ﴿dawlah﴾ with a damma on the dal and the dawlah in the accusative, according to the meaning I have mentioned, for the consensus of the authorities upon it; and the difference between dulah and dalah with damma and fatha is what I have related from the Kufan in this matter.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And whatever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives you of what Allah restored to him from the people of the towns, take it; ﴿and whatever he forbids you from﴾, such as embezzlement (ghulul) and other matters, ﴿refrain﴾. Some people of knowledge said something similar to what we have said on this, except that they directed the meaning of His saying ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ to what he gives you of the spoils.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Adi narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, refrain﴾: He said: he gives them the spoils and prevents them from embezzlement.

* *

His saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾

He says: Fear Allah, and beware of His punishment for your opposition to His Messenger by going ahead of what he has forbidden you and by disobeying him. ﴿Indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾, meaning: indeed Allah is severe in His punishment toward whoever He punishes among those who disobey His Messenger (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 8:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿For the poor emigrants who have been expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His approval, and helping Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful.﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So that it does not become a circulating wealth among the rich among you, but rather it shall be for the poor emigrants. It was also said: By "the emigrants" is meant the emigrants of Quraysh.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿what Allah bestowed upon His Messenger﴾: from Qurayza, He made it for the emigrants of Quraysh.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who both said: Some of the emigrants had a house, a wife, a servant and a camel on which he would perform the Hajj and go on raids. Allah described them as poor and assigned them a share of the zakat.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿For the poor emigrants who have been expelled from their homes﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿Those are the truthful﴾, he said: These emigrants left behind their homes, their wealth, their families and their clans, departing out of love for Allah and His Messenger, and they chose Islam despite its hardship. It has been related to us that a man would tie a stone around his stomach to keep his spine upright from hunger, and a man would dig a pit in winter, having no covering other than it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿who have been expelled from their homes and their properties﴾

And His saying: ﴿seeking bounty from Allah and His approval﴾ — the word "yabtaghuna" (seeking) is in the accusative case because it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). And His saying: ﴿and helping Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: and they support the religion of Allah with which He sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Those are the truthful﴾

He says: These, whose described qualities I have mentioned from the poor emigrants, are the truthful in what they say.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 59, verse 9:**

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And those who had homes [in Medina] and [adopted] faith before them love those who emigrate to them and find not in their breasts any need for what the emigrants were given, and they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who are the successful.﴾ (59:9)

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: ﴿And those who had homes﴾ means: they took the city, the city of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and built dwellings in it. ﴿And [adopted] faith﴾ means: in God and His Messenger. ﴿Before them﴾ means: before the emigrants. ﴿Love those who emigrate to them﴾: they love those who left their homes and moved to them from elsewhere. By this is meant the Ansar, who love the Muhajirun (emigrants).

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And those who had homes and [adopted] faith before them﴾, he said: "The Ansar" is a description. Muhammad ibn 'Amr said: "Sifatah anfusihim" (the refinement/decency of their souls). Al-Harith said: "Sakhawat anfusihim" (the generosity of their souls) in what was related from them of that, and their preferring them, and the Ansar did not receive any of that spoil.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And those who had homes and [adopted] faith before them love those who emigrate to them and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given﴾, he said: "[meaning] what they gave to their brothers, this tribe of the Ansar. They embraced Islam in their homes, and built the mosques and the mosque before the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived. So God praised them well for that. These two groups, the first in this verse, took up their virtue and passed on at their own pace, and God affirmed their share in the spoil."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God, may He be mighty and majestic: ﴿And those who had homes and [adopted] faith before them love﴾, he said: "These are the Ansar, who love those who emigrated to them from the Muhajirun."

* *

And His words: ﴿and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given﴾

His, may He be praised, says: And those who had homes before them, namely the Ansar, do not find in their breasts any need, meaning envy, for what they were given, meaning what the Muhajirun were given of the spoil. That is because it has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) divided the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir among the first Muhajirun to the exclusion of the Ansar, except two men of the Ansar whom he gave because of their poverty. He did that only as a special matter for the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, that he related that the Banu al-Nadir left their wealth to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so al-Nadir belonged to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) specifically, to place where he wished. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) divided it among the first Muhajirun, to the exclusion of the Ansar, except that Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah mentioned poverty, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave to them.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given﴾, "the Muhajirun." He said: Some of the Ansar spoke about this, [meaning] the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir, so God, may He be mighty and majestic, rebuked them for that, saying: ﴿And what God restored to His Messenger from them - you did not spur for it horse or camel. But God gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.﴾ He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "Your brothers have left their wealth and children and came out to you." They said: "Our wealth is distributed among them as estates." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Or is it other than that?" They said: "And what is that, O Messenger of God?" He said: "They are a people who do not know work, so you will provide for them and share the dates with them." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God."

Regarding His words: ﴿and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given﴾, the scholars of interpretation said the same as what we have said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sulayman Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given﴾, he said: "Envy."

He said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿need in their breasts﴾, he said: "envy in their breasts."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' informed us, from al-Hasan, the same.

* *

And His words: ﴿and they prefer them over themselves﴾

His, may He be remembered, says, describing the Ansar who had homes and [adopted] faith before the emigrants: ﴿and they prefer them over themselves﴾, meaning: they give the emigrants their wealth, preferring them with it over themselves. ﴿Even though they themselves are in privation﴾, meaning: even if they themselves had need and poverty for what they preferred of their wealth over themselves. The word khasasah is a verbal noun, and it is also a name, and it means anything through which you can see with your eye, like a niche or opening in a wall. Its plurals are khasasat and khisas, as the rajiz (rajaz poet) said:

"The women who strive (to see) know well the gap of [the] khasas..."

(This is a poem in rajaz meter whose wording is uncertain; the author cites it to show that khasas is the plural of khasasah.)

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking hospitality, but he had nothing to offer him, so he said: "Will no man host this one, may God have mercy on him?" A man of the Ansar called Abu Talhah stood up, and took him to his household, and said to his wife: "Honor the guest of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), put the children to sleep, extinguish the lamp, and show him that you are eating with him, and leave [the food] for the guest of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She did so, and [this verse] was revealed: ﴿and they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves are in privation﴾.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Fudayl, from Ghazwan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man of the Ansar hosted a guest, and he had nothing but his own food and the food of his children, so he said to his wife: "Put the children to sleep, extinguish the lamp, and bring the guest what you have." He said: So this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾, meaning: whoever God protects from the stinginess of his soul ﴿- it is those who are the successful﴾, meaning: those who abide forever in Paradise. In the speech of the Arabs, shuhh means miserliness and withholding surplus wealth. With it is the verse of 'Amr ibn Kulthum:

"You see the narrow-hearted, stingy one, when the wine is passed around to him, humbled for his wealth in it..."

(This verse is from the Mu'allaqah of 'Amr ibn Kulthum al-Taghlibi. The author cites it at the words "And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul.")

By al-shahih is meant the miserly one, one says: "He is shahih between shuhh and shahh," and there is extreme shuhh and shahahah. As for the scholars, they hold that shuhh in this place is only consuming people's wealth unjustly.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu al-Sha'tha', from his father, who said: A man came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "I fear that I have perished." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "I hear God say: 'And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul,' and I am a stingy man, hardly anything leaves my hand." He said: "That is not the stinginess that God mentioned in the Qur'an. Stinginess is only that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. That is miserliness, and miserliness is an evil thing."

Yahya ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Jami', from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, who said: A man came to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, I fear that this verse has struck me: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who are the successful﴾, and by God I do not give anything I am able to withhold." He said: "That is not stinginess; stinginess is that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. But that is miserliness."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Tariq ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi, who said: I was circumambulating the House, and I saw a man saying: "O God, protect me from the stinginess of my soul," and nothing more. I asked him about it, and he said: "When I am protected from the stinginess of my soul, I do not steal, I do not commit adultery, and I do not do anything [wrong]." The man was 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Majma' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Yazid ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "Free from stinginess is he who pays the zakat, hosts the guest, and gives in calamity."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Ziyad ibn Yunus Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Nafi' ibn 'Umar al-Makki, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: "If I escape three things, I hope to escape." 'Abd Allah ibn Safwan said: "What are they? Tell me about them." He said: "I bring out great wealth, bringing it out grudgingly, then I say: 'I will lend to my Lord tonight,' then my soul returns to it until I take it back from where I brought it out. And if I escape the matter of 'Uthman..." Ibn Safwan said: "As for 'Uthman, he was killed on the day he was killed, and you loved his killing and approved of it, so you are among those who killed him. As for you, you are a man whom God did not protect from the stinginess of his soul." He said: "You are right."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God, may He be mighty and majestic: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾, he said: "Whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, so he takes nothing from the unlawful, nor approaches it, and stinginess does not prompt him to withhold anything of the lawful, he is among the successful, as God, may He be mighty and majestic, said."

And Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾, he said: "Whoever does not take anything for a thing God forbade him, and stinginess does not leave him to withhold anything of what God commanded him, then God has protected him from the stinginess of his soul, and he is among the successful."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Compassionate and Merciful." (59:10)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And those who came after those who had settled in the abode and in faith before the first emigrants [say], "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith," [meaning] from the Ansar. By "those who came after them" He means the emigrants, that they seek forgiveness for their brothers among the Ansar.

* *

As for His saying: "and do not put in our hearts any resentment (ghill) toward those who have believed"

It means rancor (ghamr) and spite (dagh).

It has been said that by "those who came after them" is meant those who embraced Islam after those who had settled in the abode.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "And those who came after them," he said: "Those who embraced Islam later, also praised."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: Then God mentioned the third group, saying: "And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers," up to "Indeed You are Compassionate and Merciful." They were only commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and they were not commanded to speak ill of them.

It was mentioned to us that a slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, Hatib will surely enter the fire of Hell." He said: "You lie; he witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyah." It was also mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, spoke harshly to a man of the people of Badr, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "And what makes you know, O Umar? Perhaps He has looked upon the people of a scene (Badr) and said, 'Do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" So some of us remained withdrawn from the people of Badr, held in awe of them. And Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to say: "Toward the people of Badr the zealous are zealous, and as for this tribe of the Ansar, may God make their praise good."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's saying: "and do not put in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed": "Do not let our hearts inherit resentment toward anyone of your religion."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: The people were in three ranks: the first emigrants; and "those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Compassionate and Merciful." And the best that it can be is that it be in this rank.

* *

As for His saying: "toward those who have believed, our Lord, indeed You are Compassionate and Merciful"

He, exalted in praise, informs of the saying of those who came after those who had settled in the abode and in faith, that they said: "Do not place in our hearts resentment toward anyone of the people of faith in You, our Lord."

* *

As for His saying: "Indeed You are Compassionate and Merciful"

He says: You are possessed of compassion (ra'fah) toward Your creation, and possessed of mercy toward those who repent and seek forgiveness for their sins.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite, saying to their brethren among the People of the Book who disbelieved: "If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah bears witness that they are liars.﴾ [59:11]

Almighty Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Did you not look with the eye of your heart, O Muhammad, and see those who played the hypocrite? They were, as has been reported, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Wadi'a and Malik, the two sons of Nawfal, and Suwayd and Da'is. They sent word to the Banu al-Nadir when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came against them for war, saying: "Stand firm and defend yourselves, for we will not abandon you. If you are fought, we will fight alongside you, and if you are driven out, we will go out with you. So wait for their support." But they did not act, and Allah cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to exile them and to spare their blood on condition that they might take with them whatever their camels could carry of their property, except the armour.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman.

Mujahid said concerning this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite﴾. He said: Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Rifa'a or Rafi'a ibn Tabut. al-Harith said: Rifa'a ibn Tabut, and he did not doubt it, and Abd Allah ibn Nabtal, and Aws ibn Qayzi.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrima, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite﴾: he meant Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions, and those among them who held to their same affair.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿saying to their brethren among the People of the Book who disbelieved﴾

He means the Banu al-Nadir.

As reported:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrima, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿saying to their brethren among the People of the Book who disbelieved﴾, meaning: the Banu al-Nadir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you﴾

He says: Allah bears witness that these hypocrites, who promised the Banu al-Nadir support against Muhammad (ﷺ), are ﴿liars﴾ in their promise to them of what they had promised them.

They wished to travel, and it weighed on them to leave her neglected, so they began to consult about what to do with her. One of them said: "Shall I direct you to someone with whom you can leave her?" They said: "Who?" He said: "The monk of the Children of Israel. If she dies, he will attend to her, and if she lives, he will keep her safe until you return to him." The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So the consequence of both of them will be that they are in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ (18).

Exalted is He says: So the outcome of the command of Satan and of the man who obeyed him, when he disbelieved in Allah, is that both of them are abiding eternally in the Fire, remaining therein forever. ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾ means: that is the reward of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir and of the hypocrites who promised them support, and for every disbeliever in Allah who wrongs himself by his disbelief in Him, that they are eternally abiding in the Fire.

The grammarians of Arabic differed over the grammatical case of His saying ﴿khalidina fiha﴾ (abiding therein). Some grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and "in the Fire" is the predicate. He said: If it were in the speech, the nominative would be better for "khalidina." He said: The saying of people, "If you come twice" [[This phrase needs to be checked, as it contains considerable distortion and corruption.]] is accusative because of something; in it is emphasis, whether you bring it or not, it is the same, except that the Arabs often make it a circumstantial state when it carries emphasis or something similar in other places. He said: I do not prefer the nominative, though it is permissible. When you see the verb between two descriptions, one of which has returned to the place of the other, you put it in the accusative, and this is of that kind. He said: A similar example in speech is your saying: "I passed by a man on his camel, carrying it," and like the saying of the poet:

"And saffron upon his breasts, the throat-hollows and the neck's base wet with it."

Because the tara'ib are the lubab here, the description returned to the noun it had been applied to. He said: The proof by which the accusative is distinguished from the nominative is that you do not see the latter description precede the former. Do you not see that you say: "This is your brother, in his hand a dirham, grasping it"? If you said: "This is your brother, grasping it, in his hand a dirham," it would not be permissible. Do you not see that you say: "This is a man standing toward Zayd, in his hand a dirham"? * *

Exalted is He says: O you who affirmed Allah and declared His oneness, fear Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience.

* *

He says: Let each of you look at what deeds he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection, whether they are righteous deeds that will save him or evil deeds that will destroy him.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ (19)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And do not be like those who abandoned discharging the right of Allah which He made obligatory upon them, ﴿so He made them forget themselves﴾ means: Allah made them forget the portions of their own selves of good things.

And those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this.

* *

And His words: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: These who forgot Allah are the defiantly disobedient, meaning those who have left the obedience of Allah for His disobedience.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the successful.﴾ (20)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The people of the Fire and the people of Paradise are not equal; the people of Paradise are the successful, meaning that they attain what they sought and desired, and are saved from what they feared.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that they might give thought.﴾ (21)

He, may His praise be exalted, says: If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, which is a stone, you would have seen it, O Muhammad, humbled, meaning: submissive and split apart from fear of Allah despite its hardness, fearful that it might not discharge the right of Allah incumbent upon it in glorifying the Qur'an, while it has been sent down upon the son of Adam, who treats its right lightly and turns away from what it contains of lessons and remembrance, as if he had not heard it, as if there were deafness in his ears.

He says: Allah presents these examples to them so that they may reflect upon them, and so turn back (in repentance) and submit to the truth.
